topic.title: Optimal Transport and Geometry of Distributions
topic.overview: Optimal transport compares distributions by asking how much it costs to move mass between them. This topic develops computational methods and statistical guarantees for transport distances, distributional averages, and structured transport plans. Extensions compare relational spaces or allow unequal mass, making the geometry depend on more than matching individual points.
topic.whyItMatters: Transport provides a common language for distribution comparison, clustering, and adaptation, but exact computation can be expensive. Regularization, slicing, and low-rank structure improve tractability while changing the optimization problem or the information retained. Those trade-offs must be interpreted alongside statistical estimation error.
topic.evolution: A 2012 representative connects transport-based measure estimation with quantization and learning theory. Sinkhorn computation and Wasserstein barycenters appear in subsequent work. A 2021 study extends Gromov-Wasserstein comparison to arbitrary positive measures; 2026 transport clustering gives approximation algorithms for low-rank plans through a reduction to clustering correspondences.
openQuestions: When does low-rank transport preserve the structure relevant to a downstream task?
How should regularization balance computational speed against geometric distortion?
